items.text: REFERRED TO COMMERCE, ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AND SMALL BUSINESS

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S3492

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the alcoholic beverage control law, in relation to
authorizing farm wineries to store and sell the equipment and supplies
used for wine-making

 PURPOSE :
To make it very clear that the Alcoholic Beverage Control Law
authorizes farm wineries to sell wine-making kits, equipment, and
supplies to all wine-makers and to home wine-makers on the premises of
a farm winery.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :
Section 1: Amends Alcoholic Beverage Control Law section 76-a(4) to
make it very clear that farm wineries can sell wine-making equipment,
supplies, grapes and grape juice to both commercial and home
wine-makers.

 EXISTING LAW :
Under current law, it is very much implied that farm wineries may sell
home wine-making equipment and supplies to individuals to make wine in
their homes for home consumption and to other wine-makers. However,
some have suggested that the law should be made very clear to ensure
that this practice can be conducted on the premises of a farm winery.

 JUSTIFICATION :
This bill ensures that farm wineries can conduct ancillary businesses
that complement their main business purpose which is to produce wines
from New York grown grapes. Increasing the number of ancillary
businesses that a farm winery can clearly conduct on their property
can increase the overall business opportunities available to these
companies and thereby, increase their overall profitability.

This bill was amended to retain language related to selling gift items
at the winery.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
A10321A of 2008

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.
